hints: Remember what makes a catalyst special, it gets used up in one step but is made again in a later step so there is no net change.
Look closely at the first two equations, $\text{NO}_2$ is broken down to make $\text{NO}$, then that same $\text{NO}$ reacts to remake $\text{NO}_2$.
Add the first two steps together and cancel species that appear on both sides to see the overall change, then check which nitrogen oxides are left over.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for a catalyst**

A catalyst speeds up a reaction but is not used up overall. It is consumed in an early step and regenerated in a later step.

Rule to check:
$$\text{catalyst used up} \rightarrow \text{catalyst remade, net change = 0}$$

**Track NO2 and NO through the first two steps**

In step 1, $\text{NO}_2$ is used up:
$$\text{NO}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{NO}(g) + \text{O}(g)$$
In step 2, that $\text{NO}$ is used up to remake $\text{NO}_2$:
$$\text{NO}(g) + \tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{NO}_2(g)$$

**Add the steps to find the net reaction**

Add steps 1 and 2 and cancel $\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$ which appear on both sides:
$$\tfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{O}(g)$$
Then step 3 uses that $\text{O}$ atom:
$$\text{O}_2(g) + \text{O}(g) \rightarrow \text{O}_3(g)$$
Overall, oxygen is converted to ozone, while $\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$ have no net change.

**Conclude who is the catalyst**

Because both $\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$ are consumed and then regenerated, and the sequence can repeat many times, both fit the definition of a catalyst.

options.A: This is only half right. $\text{NO}$ is regenerated in step 1 after being used in step 2, so it is a catalyst. But $\text{NO}_2$ is also regenerated in step 2 after being used in step 1, so it cannot be excluded.
options.B: This is only half right. $\text{NO}_2$ is regenerated in step 2 after being used in step 1, so it is a catalyst. But $\text{NO}$ is also regenerated in step 1 after being used in step 2, so it cannot be excluded.
options.C: This misses the cycle. Both species appear as a product in one step and a reactant in the other, so there is no net consumption of either. That is exactly catalytic behaviour, not non-catalytic.
options.D: Correct. $\text{NO}_2$ is used in step 1 and remade in step 2, while $\text{NO}$ is made in step 1 and used in step 2. Neither is used up overall and both help produce $\text{O}$ atoms for ozone formation, so both act as catalysts.
